summary: Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956). His career included posts at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (1988–2006), and several universities.

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895) and later served there as professor emeritus (~1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani (born 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University and at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama (1995), later serving as professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Linguist Tadeusz Milewski (1906–1966) earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lviv and studied at Jagiellonian University under Jan Michał Rozwadowski, Helena Willman-Grabowska, Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Émile Benveniste. He held professorships at Lublin (1945–1950) and Jagiellonian University (1949–1966).

Tadeusz Pobożniak (1910–1991) worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at Jagiellonian University, studying under Helena Willman-Grabowska and Jan Michał Rozwadowski, and served as professor at Jagiellonian University (~1954–1975).

Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of London (1978), he served as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005) at SOAS University of London.

Tai-shing Wut specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998) and served as assistant professor at City University of Hong Kong (2009–2014).
Taido Kitamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts at Shuchiin University, including assistant professor (attested 1980) and later affiliation attested 1994–1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Columbia University and Graduate Theological Union (Ph.D. ~1994–2000), he held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (~2008).

Taijun Inokuchi (1930–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held several posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987), becoming professor emeritus by 1996.

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, later becoming professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1912.

Taiken Kyuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from Ryukoku University in 2016, where he also served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Koyasan University and Toyo University (Ph.D. 1994), and served as an assistant professor and professor at Koyasan University (attested 1980–2026).
Taion Satomi (born 1909) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (graduated 1933) and served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a historian and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1919) and Tokyo University of Education (~1902–1919).

Tairyo Makita (1912–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1949–1976), Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~1977–1988), and president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997).
Tairyū Tsunoda (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
